column1: # corpus for modules/image/distro/rpm_version.sh - the rpm version
# comparator, the second ticket of the rpm sub-chain IMG-12's enumerator
# FORMAT: four TAB-separated columns, `A <op> B <why>`, where <op> is one of
# and tests/fixtures/image/dpkg-version-corpus.tsv use, and a one-for-one map
# onto `rpmdev-vercmp`'s own exit codes (0 equal, 11 A newer, 12 B newer), so
# the follow-up live differential named in the comparator's header is a direct
# column diff rather than a translation.  Whole-line `#` comments and blank
# lines are ignored, matching the record-format instinct the rest of this
# repository uses; a value never needs escaping because no column can contain
# a TAB and no legal rpm version can contain one either.
# PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY.  Rows here come from three places and nowhere
#      measured `modules/sca/semver.sh` getting WRONG.  These are the rows
#      this ticket exists for and they are marked (report.md 2.4).
#   2. rpm's OWN PUBLISHED TEST VECTORS - the pairs librpm's `rpmvercmp.at`
#      asserts - transcribed by hand and marked (rpm vector).  They are the
#      closest thing to a harvested corpus available offline: each one is a
#      pair the tool's maintainers wrote down as the answer.
#   3. Cases derived from rpm's documented `rpmvercmp` algorithm, covering
#      each rule the other two do not reach on its own, marked with the rule
# NONE of it was harvested by running `rpmdev-vercmp` or `rpm`: scoursh is
# egress-restricted and the development host has neither binary, so a live
# harvest of the shape `modules/sca/semver.sh` used for npm was not
# available.  This is the strongest OFFLINE corpus available and it is not a
# substitute for that run - see the comparator's own "THE OFFLINE-CORPUS
# LIMIT" section for the follow-up hardening this owes.
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT.  rpm's own vector file carries a block of
# NON-ASCII rows (`1.1.<alpha>` compares EQUAL to `1.1.<beta>`, because
# rpm's `risalnum` is ASCII-only and skips a UTF-8 byte as a separator)
# under a comment calling them "arguably buggy behaviors ... included here
# to document current behavior".  This comparator REFUSES a non-ASCII byte
# rather than reproducing a documented bug that makes two genuinely
# different versions indistinguishable, so those rows cannot appear in a
# file every row of which must be orderable.  The refusal is pinned in
# tests/suites/image-rpm-version.sh section C instead, naming rpm's own
# answer, so the divergence is measured rather than merely absent.
